st: If the pork is very salty, soak it in cold water for 2 hours first, then drain.
Put the pork in a pot, cover with fresh cold water, add the bay leaves, and bring to a gentle simmer. Cook covered for 1 hour 15 minutes until tender, reaching at least 145°F (63°C).
If using fresh fava beans, boil them in salted water for 3 minutes, cool, and slip off the tough outer skins. Frozen beans just need thawing.
Add the potatoes to the pot with the pork for the last 20 minutes of cooking.
Fry the bacon in a large skillet for 5 minutes. Add the onion and [[2 tbsp]] butter and cook 5 minutes until soft.
Stir in [[1 tbsp]] flour for 1 minute, then add the beans and about a cup of the pork cooking liquid. Simmer for 10 minutes.
Stir in [[0.5 cup]] cream and the pepper and simmer for 3 minutes. Taste and add salt if needed.
Slice the pork, spoon the beans over it and serve with the potatoes, sprinkled with the parsley.
Trim the beans and cut them into 1-inch pieces. Peel and cube the potatoes.
Cook the bacon in a large pot over medium heat for 6 minutes until the fat melts.
Add the onion and leek and cook for 5 minutes until soft.
Pour in [[5 cups]] broth and add the bay leaf and the pepper. Bring to a boil.
Add the potatoes and cook for 10 minutes.
Add the beans and the sausage and simmer for 15 minutes until the beans are tender.
Remove the bay leaf. Stir in [[0.5 cup]] cream and heat gently for 3 minutes without boiling.
Taste for salt, sprinkle with the parsley and serve hot with bread.
Grate the potatoes and the onion on the coarse side of a box grater into a bowl.
Squeeze the mix hard in a clean towel to remove as much liquid as possible, then return it to a dry bowl.
Add the eggs, [[3 tbsp]] flour, [[3 tbsp]] parsley, [[1 tsp]] salt and the pepper and stir well.
Heat [[0.5 cup]] oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat until it shimmers.
Drop heaped spoonfuls of the mix into the oil and flatten to thin patties. Do not crowd the pan.
Fry for 4 minutes per side until deep golden and crisp at the edges.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot with applesauce or a green salad.

ing: dry white wine; use chicken broth if avoiding alcohol
st: Mix the pork, veal, onion, parsley, thyme, [[1.5 tsp]] salt and [[0.75 tsp]] pepper. Pour over [[0.5 cup]] Riesling, cover, and marinate in the fridge for 4 hours.
Hard boil 1 egg for 10 minutes, cool, peel and slice it.
Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Line a baking sheet with parchment and lay out 1 sheet of pastry.
Pile the meat mix on the pastry, leaving a 1-inch border, tucking in the egg slices. Brush the border with beaten egg.
Cover with the second pastry sheet, press the edges to seal and trim. Brush the top with egg and cut a small round hole in the center.
Bake for 20 minutes, then reduce the oven to 350°F (175°C) and bake 50 minutes more until deep golden and the meat reaches 160°F (71°C).
Meanwhile sprinkle the gelatin over [[0.5 cup]] broth for 5 minutes, warm until dissolved, then add the remaining [[0.5 cup]] Riesling.
Cool the pie for 20 minutes, then slowly pour the aspic liquid through the hole in the top.
Chill the pie for at least 4 hours until the aspic sets, then slice cold.
Whisk [[2 cups]] flour, [[1 tsp]] salt and [[0.25 tsp]] nutmeg in a bowl.
Add the eggs and [[0.75 cup]] milk and beat for 2 minutes to a thick, sticky dough.
Rest the dough for 10 minutes. Meanwhile bring a large pot of salted water to a gentle boil.
Using two wet teaspoons, scoop small pieces of dough and drop them in the water.
Cook for 5 minutes. They are done when they float and feel firm.
Lift out with a slotted spoon and drain well.
Fry the bacon in a large skillet for 6 minutes until crisp. Add [[3 tbsp]] butter.
Add the dumplings and fry for 5 minutes, turning, until golden at the edges. Season with the pepper and serve.

ing: pitted and halved, or Italian prune plums
st: Mix [[1.5 cups]] flour, [[0.25 cup]] sugar and a pinch of salt. Rub in [[0.5 cup]] cold butter until crumbly.
Stir in the egg and about [[2 tbsp]] cold water until the dough comes together. Wrap and chill for 30 minutes.
Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C).
Roll the dough out and fit it into a 9-inch tart pan, trimming the edge. Prick the base with a fork.
Arrange the plum halves skin-side down in tight overlapping circles, cut sides facing up.
Mix the remaining [[0.25 cup]] sugar with [[1 tsp]] cinnamon and sprinkle it over the plums.
Bake for 40 minutes until the crust is golden and the plums are soft and bubbling.
Cool for 30 minutes before slicing. Serve warm or at room temperature.
Put the beef in a pot, cover with water, add the bay leaf and [[1 tsp]] salt. Bring to a boil, skim, then simmer covered for 2 hours until very tender.
Lift the beef out, let it cool for 30 minutes, then slice it thinly and cut into strips.
Hard boil the eggs for 10 minutes, cool, peel and chop.
Whisk [[1 tbsp]] mustard with [[3 tbsp]] vinegar, then whisk in [[0.25 cup]] oil in a thin stream with the pepper.
Combine the beef, onion, pickles and chopped eggs in a bowl.
Pour the dressing over and toss gently.
Chill for 30 minutes so the flavors blend.
Taste for salt, sprinkle with the parsley and serve cold with bread.
